programmes.source_snippet: The Adult Migrant English Program (AMEP) is a free service to help eligible migrants and humanitarian entrants improve their English language skills and settle into Australia.

programmes.funder: Department of Health, Disability and Ageing (My Aged Care)
programmes.amount_note: Government-funded in-home aged care (nursing, personal care, domestic help, meals, transport, equipment, home modifications). Funding is assigned by one of 8 classifications after assessment; you contribute to some services based on income and assets, and from 1 October 2026 personal care is fully government-funded.

procedure_steps.detail: Check if you are eligible and apply for an aged care assessment through My Aged Care
Receive an approval letter with your services and funding
Choose a provider and sign a service agreement

documents_required.doc: Income and asset information for Services Australia (to work out contributions)

eligibility.income_note: Eligibility is by aged care assessment of care needs, not by an income cut-off; income and assets only determine the contribution you pay.

programmes.source_snippet: The Support at Home program was introduced in November 2025, replacing the Home Care Packages Program and the Short-term Restorative Care Programme.

programmes.funder: Australian Government (DCCEEW, via the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme)
programmes.amount_note: From 1 July 2025 the Australian Government funds around a 30% discount on eligible small-scale battery systems connected to new or existing rooftop solar. The discount is generally provided via solar and battery retailers and installers.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose an eligible battery system and an approved installer/retailer
The discount is applied at purchase by the retailer or installer

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested. Applies to households and small businesses installing an eligible battery with rooftop solar.

programmes.source_snippet: From 1 July 2025, the Australian Government is funding around a 30% discount on eligible small-scale battery systems connected to new or existing rooftop solar.

programmes.funder: NSW Government (Service NSW / NSW Energy Rebates)
programmes.amount_note: Lump-sum rebate credited to your electricity bill to help families with dependent children. One rebate per household per financial year; principal place of residence only. Dollar amount is set by the NSW Government each year.
programmes.deadline_note: Processing currently 6 to 8 weeks

procedure_steps.detail: Make sure your 2025-26 tax return is lodged and your Family Tax Benefit is finalised with Centrelink
Apply online via Service NSW (or post the PDF form with your latest electricity bill)

documents_required.doc: Services Australia letter confirming Family Tax Benefit finalised

eligibility.income_note: No separate income figure: you must have received Family Tax Benefit in 2025-26, which is itself income-tested.

programmes.source_snippet: The NSW Family Energy Rebate helps people with dependent children pay their electricity bills.

programmes.funder: Victorian Department of Families, Fairness and Housing
programmes.amount_note: Grant towards an overdue mains electricity, gas or water bill. Maximum $650 per utility type in a two-year period ($1,300 for households with a single source of energy); paid to your retailer.

procedure_steps.detail: Phone your electricity, gas or water retailer to request an application
Complete the form online or on paper (a support worker can help) and return it

documents_required.doc: Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card or DVA Gold Card (or other proof of low income)
Payslips, receipts or statutory declaration as needed

eligibility.income_note: No published dollar ceiling: account holder must hold a Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card or DVA Gold Card, or be part of a low-income household, and meet a hardship criterion (family violence, recent income drop, high unexpected costs, or shelter costs above 30% of household income).

programmes.source_snippet: Relief grants for paying overdue energy or water bills are available to low-income Victorians experiencing unexpected hardship.

programmes.amount_note: Subsidy of 20 per cent (up to a maximum of $200 each year) of the gross rates and charges levied by your local council.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your local council to apply (each council has its own process)
Lodge a new application if you change address

documents_required.doc: Queensland Pensioner Concession Card or DVA Gold Card

eligibility.income_note: Not a separate income test: you must hold a Pensioner Concession Card or DVA Gold Card (which are income- and assets-tested) and own or be life tenant of your Queensland home.

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible pensioners can receive a subsidy of 20 per cent (up to a maximum amount of $200 each year) of the gross rates and charges levied by your local council.

programmes.funder: Australian Government (DEWR) with state and territory governments
programmes.amount_note: Tuition-free TAFE and vocational education places in priority areas (care, technology, hospitality, construction, agriculture, manufacturing, VET workforce). Made permanent by the Free TAFE Act 2025, with at least 100,000 places per year from 2027.
programmes.deadline_note: Places and eligibility are set by each state and territory; check Your Career for current courses

procedure_steps.detail: Search eligible Free TAFE courses on Your Career
Enrol with your state or territory TAFE provider

documents_required.doc: Proof of identity and residency/visa status

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; places are prioritised for First Nations Australians, people aged 17-24, people out of work or on income support, unpaid carers, women facing economic insecurity, people with disability and certain visa holders.

programmes.source_snippet: The Australian Government has made Free TAFE a permanent feature of the national VET system

programmes.amount_note: Case-managed settlement support for 6-18 months: airport reception, short-term accommodation, help finding long-term housing, learning English, employment, education and training, and orientation.

procedure_steps.detail: Granted a Refugee (subclass 200, 201, 203, 204) or Global Special Humanitarian (subclass 202) visa; support starts on arrival
Work with your HSP service provider case manager

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; based on visa type. Australian citizens are not eligible. Subclass 202 visa holders under the Community Support Program are supported by their proposing organisation instead.

programmes.source_snippet: The Humanitarian Settlement Program (HSP) supports humanitarian entrants and other eligible visa holders during their initial settlement.

programmes.amount_note: Rebate amount depends on the life support machine and the number of days in the billing period.
programmes.deadline_note: Reapply every 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Get the form completed by a medical practitioner
Submit it to your electricity retailer

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested.

programmes.source_snippet: Apply through the electricity retailer with a medical practitioner's form.

programmes.name_local: Queensland Home Energy Emergency Assistance Scheme
programmes.name_en: Queensland Home Energy Emergency Assistance Scheme
programmes.amount_note: Up to $720 once every 2 years towards energy bills.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your energy provider
Complete the online application form

documents_required.doc: Concession card or proof of income/hardship

eligibility.income_note: Eligible with a concession card, income at or below the part-rate age pension limit, or being on a hardship programme; no single ceiling published here.

programmes.source_snippet: Up to $720 once every 2 years.

programmes.amount_note: Free kindergarten for 3- and 4-year-old children.

procedure_steps.detail: Find a kinder programme near you
Enrol with the chosen service

documents_required.doc: Child's birth certificate or proof of age

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested.

programmes.source_snippet: Free Kinder: All 3- and 4-year-old children in Victoria can access Free Kinder.

programmes.amount_note: 15 hours per week for 40 weeks per year of free kindergarten.

procedure_steps.detail: Check the child meets the age cut-off
Enrol with an approved kindergarten provider

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested. Refugee and humanitarian visa families and fee-exempt temporary visa holders are eligible.

programmes.source_snippet: 15 hours per week for 40 weeks per year, for children at least 4 by 30 June in the year before school.
